mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a backyard sauna in Whitby?

acceptedAnswer.text: An accessory building over 10 m² typically needs a building permit, zoning setbacks apply, and the electrical connection needs an ESA permit. We check your lot and model before you order.

mainEntity.name: Is a sauna OK close to Lake Ontario?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Cedar handles damp air well. We recommend a sheltered location, a well-drained base, and exterior oil to protect the wood from UV and weather.

mainEntity.name: Can you install a cold plunge with my sauna?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We sell cold plunges and can plan both together.

mainEntity.name: How much does delivery and installation cost in Whitby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delivery and installation is $1,750 anywhere in Ontario, including Whitby. Delivery only is $450. HST is shown separately on every quote.

mainEntity.name: What heater size does my sauna need?

acceptedAnswer.text: We size every heater to the sauna's interior volume plus extra for glass. None of our saunas take less than a 6 kW heater; larger models use 9 to 10.5 kW electric or a wood stove where there's room for its clearances.

blocks.html: Lakefront neighbourhoods like Port Whitby and Lynde Shores get stronger winds and damp winter air off Lake Ontario. Our cedar saunas handle it well; for exposed lots we recommend a sheltered spot and a well-drained base.
